text:
**Short answer:** the Anker Prime 26K (300W) is the best overall pick. If you want to spend less, the Baseus Blade H1 is a good 100W option for a 14-inch MacBook Pro.

## What to look for
- **16-inch MacBook Pro:** get a PD 3.1 bank with a 140W port. Macworld says to pair it with Apple's USB-C to MagSafe 3 cable, or a Thunderbolt 5 cable on M4/M5 models, for full-speed charging. Over a regular USB-C connection it tops out at 100W. ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/819438/best-macbook-usb-c-charger.html))
- **14-inch MacBook Pro:** about 96W or more fast-charges it, so a 100W bank is enough. (same source)
- **Flying:** airlines cap carry-on batteries at 100Wh, so most big banks sit just under that. ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/2955100/ecoflow-rapid-pro-27k-power-bank-300w-review-macbook-battery-pack.html))

## Top picks

**Best overall: Anker Prime Power Bank (26,250mAh, 300W)**, about $200–$230
- It has two 140W USB-C ports, 300W total output, and 99.75Wh capacity, so it's airline-legal.
- In Macworld's test it charged a 14-inch M2 MacBook Pro fully and then took it back to 25%.
- WIRED also rates it highly. Its downside is that it has no built-in cable, though a USB-C cable is included.
- [Macworld review and prices](https://www.macworld.com/article/2395511/best-laptop-power-banks-for-apple-macbook.html) · [WIRED roundup with Amazon/Anker links](https://www.wired.com/story/best-laptop-power-banks/)

**Best with a built-in cable: EcoFlow RAPID Pro 27K (300W)**, about $190–$220
- It has a retractable cable rated at 140W, plus two 140W and two 65W USB-C ports.
- Capacity is 99.54Wh, and it recharges to 80% in about 30–40 minutes.
- Macworld estimates it can recharge a laptop to about 70–75% in practice. Prices vary by retailer.
- [Macworld review](https://www.macworld.com/article/2955100/ecoflow-rapid-pro-27k-power-bank-300w-review-macbook-battery-pack.html) · [WIRED roundup](https://www.wired.com/story/best-laptop-power-banks/)

**Best value: ReelCharge ReelPro (27,000mAh, 200W)**, about $120
- It has a built-in cable rated at 140W and one USB-C and one USB-A port, both at 100W.
- ReelCharge is a new brand, which WIRED notes is a bit riskier. The warranty is 3 years.
- [WIRED roundup](https://www.wired.com/story/best-laptop-power-banks/)

**Budget 100W option: Baseus Blade H1 (20,000mAh, 100W)**, $89.99
- It's flat, about 74Wh, and comes with a 100W cable.
- It works well for a 14-inch Pro, but it won't fast-charge a 16-inch Pro at 140W. Maximum input is 60W, so recharging the bank itself is slower.
- The Baseus warranty is 24 months.
- [Buy at Baseus via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah) (an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you; the price was verified 2026-10-21 and checkout is the final word.)

## Also worth a look
The INIU Cougar P64 (140W) is a lower-cost PD 3.1 option, per [Macworld's list](https://www.macworld.com/article/2395511/best-laptop-power-banks-for-apple-macbook.html), but I didn't see a price in the results. The Anker 737 (24,000mAh, 140W, 86.4Wh) is another proven choice in [Laptopbee's roundup](https://www.laptopbee.com/best-power-banks-for-macbook-pro/), a less rigorous source than the others.

**My pick:** the Anker Prime 26K if you have a 16-inch Pro or want the best all-rounder. The Baseus Blade H1 is the cheaper choice if you have a 14-inch Pro and just need one solid recharge on the go.

Which MacBook Pro size do you have? I can narrow it down from there.
